card.statement:
(a) Over an algebraically closed field $\mathbb F$ with nonidentity involution represented in the form <<ref:1pp11>>, every pair $(A,B)$ of Hermitian matrices of the same size is *congruent to a direct sum, determined uniquely up to permutation of summands, of tridiagonal pairs of two types:

\begin{equation}
\left(\begin{bmatrix}
0&1&&&0\\
1&0&1\\
&1&0&\ddots\\
&&\ddots&\ddots&1\\
0&&&1&0
\end{bmatrix}_{n},\
\begin{bmatrix}
0&\mu &&&0\\
\bar\mu &0&\mu \\
&\bar\mu &0&\ddots\\
&&\ddots&\ddots&\mu \\
0&&&\bar\mu &0
\end{bmatrix}_{n}\right),
\end{equation}

in which $\mu\in\mathbb
F\smallsetminus\mathbb
P$ if $n$ is even, $\mu=\pm i$ if $n$ is odd, and $\mu$ is determined up to replacement by $\bar\mu$; and

\begin{equation}
\left(\begin{bmatrix}
a &b&&&&0\\
b&0&a\\
&a&0&b\\
&&b&0&a\\
&&&a&0&\ddots\\
0&&&&\ddots&\ddots
\end{bmatrix}_n,\
\begin{bmatrix}
b&-a&&&&0\\
-a&0&b\\
&b&0&-a\\
&&-a&0&b\\
&&&b&0&\ddots\\
0&&&&\ddots&\ddots
\end{bmatrix}_n\;\right),
\end{equation}

in which $a,b\in\mathbb P$ and $a^2+b^2=1$.

(b) The Kronecker canonical form of $(A,B)$ under equivalence determines this direct sum uniquely up to permutation of summands and multiplication by $-1$ any direct summand of type <<ref:he2>>. The Kronecker canonical form of each of the direct summands is given in the following table:

\begin{equation}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline
Pair& Kronecker
canonical form of the
pair
\\
\hline\hline
<<ref:he1>>&
$\begin{array}{rl}
(F_k,G_k)\oplus
(F_k^T,G_k^T)
&\text{if $n=2k+1$}\\
(I_k,J_k(\mu)) \oplus
(I_k,J_k(\bar\mu))
&\text{if $n=2k$}
\end{array}$
\\\hline
<<ref:he2>>&
$\begin{array}{rl}
(I_n,J_n( b/a))
&\text{if $n$ is odd
and $a\ne 0$}\\
(I_n,J_n(-a/b))
&\text{if $n$ is even
and $b\ne 0$}\\
(J_n(0),I_n)
&\text{otherwise}
\end{array}$
\\\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{equation}
card.label: Theorem 7

paper.title: Tridiagonal canonical matrices of bilinear or sesquilinear forms and of pairs of symmetric, skew-symmetric, or Hermitian forms
paper.abstract: Tridiagonal canonical forms of square matrices under congruence or *congruence, pairs of symmetric or skew-symmetric matrices under congruence, and pairs of Hermitian matrices under *congruence are given over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2.
